title: Connect your AI Agent to Help Scout via MCP
snippet:
Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access to Help Scout data. You can connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and your own internal AI tools directly to Help Scout to pull up conversations, customer details, mailbox data, and Docs content. This integration is available on the Standard, Plus, and Pro plans — any plan that includes Help Scout API access. Report tools require Plus or Pro. Access is read-only for new connections, and each team member connects with their own Help Scout credentials, ensuring your AI Agent only accesses data that the specific user is permitted to see.

Help Scout isn't listed in Claude's connector directory yet; it's added as a custom connector using a server URL. How you add it depends on your Claude plan.
### **Team and Enterprise plans**
Only a Claude Owner can add a custom connector. Ask your Owner to:
1. Go to Organization settings > Connectors.
2. Click **Add**, hover over **Custom**, then select **Web**.
Set the remote MCP server URL to `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp` .
1. Leave Advanced settings empty. The OAuth Client ID and Client Secret fields are optional; the connector registers itself. Don't enter a Help Scout App ID or secret from My Apps here; those are for the Help Scout API and won't work for the connector.
3. Click **Add**.
Once the connector is added, each team member connects individually:
1. Go to Customize > Connectors.
2. Find Help Scout in the list — it has a **Custom** label.
3. Click **Connect**, then log in to Help Scout and approve access.

1. Name the connector **Help Scout**.
Set the remote MCP server URL to `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp` .
1. Leave Advanced settings empty. The OAuth Client ID and Client Secret fields are optional; the connector registers itself. Don't enter a Help Scout App ID or secret from My Apps here; those are for the Help Scout API and won't work for the connector.
2. Click **Add**.

ChatGPT adds custom MCP connectors through developer mode, so you'll see a standard warning when you turn it on. That warning applies to custom connectors in general, not to anything specific to Help Scout. To get things set up:
1. In ChatGPT, go to Settings > Security and login and turn on Developer mode. On Business, Enterprise, and Education workspaces, your workspace admin needs to approve it first.

1. Go to Plugins (or open chatgpt.com/plugins) and click the + button to add a new connector.

title: Help Scout's MCP server is now available
snippet:
Today, we're bringing Help Scout's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server out of beta, making it generally available to all Help Scout customers.

With Help Scout's MCP server, AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor can securely retrieve the customer knowledge already stored in your Help Scout account. Instead of manually searching through conversations, you can simply ask questions like:
- What product issues has this customer reported over the last six months?
- Summarize the feature requests we've received from our top customers over the past quarter.
- Show me every conversation related to this account from the last 90 days.
- Find every conversation mentioning damaged orders from the past 30 days.
- Which issues generated the highest volume in our general inbox this week?

#### **Available today: Read-only access**
Giving AI access to customer conversations requires the right safeguards. That's why the first generally available version of MCP is intentionally read-only. Each team member connects using their own Help Scout credentials, ensuring AI assistants can only access the conversations and customer data that person is already authorized to view. MCP respects your existing permissions, giving teams confidence that customer knowledge stays secure while it becomes more accessible.
#### **From context to action**
Read access is the first capability available through Help Scout's MCP server, and it's only the beginning. As teams become more comfortable bringing customer context into their AI workflows, the next step is helping them act on that context. Over time, we will introduce write capabilities that support common support workflows, allowing AI to help draft replies, organize conversations, add internal notes, and complete other routine tasks inside Help Scout.

title: Help Scout MCP Server (2026): Official, Setup for Claude, Cursor & VS Code
snippet:
# Help Scout MCP server
Help Scout has an official MCP server: Hosted server to search Help Scout conversations and pull support reports. Below is the server with the setup for 13 clients: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and more. Checked 2026-10-24 against each project's own repo, docs and the official MCP Registry.
Hosted server to search Help Scout conversations and pull support reports.
https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp
Run in a terminal, then /mcp inside Claude Code to sign in. Add --scope project to share it via .mcp.json. [docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)
```
claude mcp add --transport http help-scout https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp
```

Yes: Help Scout, maintained by Help Scout.
In Claude Code run: claude mcp add --transport http help-scout https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp, then /mcp to sign in. In Claude Desktop or claude.ai, go to Customize > Connectors > Add > Add custom connector and paste https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp.
Open the Cursor or VS Code tab on the server above: it has the exact mcp.json entry and a one-click install link. The same server also works in Claude Code, Claude Desktop / claude.ai, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and Codex.
ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers only. Help Scout has a hosted URL: at chatgpt.com/plugins choose + > Add custom MCP server, paste the URL and create it as a plugin.
Start with the official server, a read-only or test account and approval prompts on for anything that writes. Content the agent reads from Help Scout (tickets, messages, pages) can carry prompt-injection instructions, so don't auto-approve actions.

title: help-scout-mcp-server/README.md at main · drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server
snippet:
An [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) that gives AI assistants direct access to your Help Scout inboxes, conversations, customers, organizations, threads, and Docs knowledge base. Search tickets, pull customer and account context, inspect articles, spot patterns, and get answers without leaving your editor or chat window.
Built by a Help Scout customer who wanted to give his support team superpowers. If you handle customer conversations in Help Scout and want AI to help you work faster, this is for you.
## What You Can Do
- **Search conversations** by keyword, date range, status, tag, email domain, or ticket number
- **Look up customers** by name, advanced query syntax, or exact email address
- **Explore organizations** with direct customer and conversation traversal
- **Inspect conversation detail** with raw ticket metadata, summaries, full threads, attachments, and original source
- **Pull full thread history** into context before drafting a reply
- **Get conversation summaries** with the original customer message and latest staff response
- **Search and retrieve Docs articles** from the separate Help Scout Docs API
- **Pull Help Scout reports and metadata** for company, conversations, Docs, channels, productivity, happiness, users, teams, system users, statuses, routing, and webhooks
- **Monitor inbox activity** across multiple inboxes with a single query
- **Take action with opt-in writes**: draft replies, internal notes, tags, status, assignment, snooze, and more, all off by default
- **Reduce message payloads** with optional message content redaction and scoped inbox access
## Quick Start
### Claude Desktop & Claude Cowork (Recommended)
**One-click install** using [Desktop Extensions](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/desktop-extensions). One install covers both Chat and Cowork sessions in the Claude desktop app.
1. Download the latest [`.mcpb` file from releases](https://github.com/drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server/releases)
2. Double-click to install (or drag into Claude Desktop)
3. Enter your Help Scout App ID and App Secret in the extension settings; the settings also carry toggles for message redaction and the opt-in write surface
4. Restart Claude Desktop
If the tools don't show up in a Cowork session, update the desktop app to the latest version and start a fresh session. ([Cowork walkthrough](/drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server/blob/main/guides/cowork-setup.md))
Optional: add the **helpscout-navigator** skill so Claude pic

title: Help Scout's AI Features: Deliver Better Support, Faster
snippet:
The features above bring AI into Help Scout. [Help Scout's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](https://docs.helpscout.com/article/1779-connect-your-ai-agent-with-help-scout-to-search-conversations-and-pull-reports) does the opposite: it brings your Help Scout customer knowledge into the AI tools your team already uses.
Your help desk is one of the richest sources of customer knowledge in your entire business, but manually reviewing dozens, hundreds, or thousands of historical conversations is impractical. Help Scout's MCP server lets AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor securely retrieve that customer knowledge. You can use it to get information like:
- The most common questions customers ask that aren't yet covered in your knowledge base.
- Which topics or products are driving the biggest week-over-week increase in conversation volume.
- Every mention of a competitor across your conversations over the past quarter.
- The objections or hesitations prospects raise most often before purchasing.
- A summary of what a specific customer has contacted you about before your next call with them.
- The feature requests that are most frequently tied to your highest-value accounts.
Access is currently read-only. Each team member connects using their own Help Scout credentials, so AI assistants can only ever access the conversations and customer data that person is authorized to view.

title: Help Scout MCP Server: Tools, Setup and Security
snippet:
Help Scout's official MCP connector gives AI apps read-only access to conversations, customers, reports and Docs. Plans, Claude and ChatGPT setup, data notes.

The Help Scout MCP connector lets an AI app search and summarize support conversations, look up customer profiles, and pull company, productivity and happiness reports. It can also search Help Scout Docs articles. Help Scout publishes and hosts it, and as of October 2026 access is read-only for new connections.

- The server URL is `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp`, and each team member signs in with their own Help Scout account.
- New connections are read-only. The AI cannot reply to customers, add notes, change tags or edit Docs.
- It is available on the Standard, Plus and Pro plans. Report tools need Plus or Pro.
- Help Scout has no account-wide switch to turn MCP off. Any User or Administrator can connect.
- The connector does not strip sensitive information, so whatever customers wrote reaches the AI.
## At a glance
| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Publisher | Help Scout |
| Official? | Yes |
| Hosting | Remote URL: `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp` |
| Transport | Not stated |
| Sign-in | OAuth (each user signs in on Help Scout's page) |
| Read or write | Read-only for new connections |
| Price | No separate MCP price listed; Standard, Plus or Pro plan required |
| Source code | Closed (hosted by Help Scout) |
| Status | Generally available, per Help Scout |
## What it can do
Help Scout's article describes capability groups rather than tool names:
- **Conversations:** list, search and summarize conversations, including threads, tags, custom fields and attachment file names. It cannot open attachment contents.
- **Customers:** profiles, emails, phone numbers, history and organizations.
- **Inboxes and saved replies.**
- **Users and teams.**
- **Workflows.**
- **Reports:** company, conversation, productivity and happiness reports, on Plus or Pro.
- **Docs:** search and read articles, sites and collections, if you add a Docs API key.

Help Scout documents three paths:
**Claude Team or Enterprise:** a Claude Owner adds a custom web connector under Organization settings > Connectors using the server URL. Each member then clicks Connect under Customize > Connectors.
**Claude Pro or Max:** go to Customize > Connectors, choose Add custom connector, name it "Help Scout," enter `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp`, click Add, then log in and approve.
